sentences.zh: 我们是怎么从《豪门恩怨》中

sentences.en: around with is the ABC sitcom Modern Family.
sentences.zh: 是ABC的情景喜剧《摩登家庭》。

sentences.zh: 比如《生活大爆炸》，以及诸如《罗斯安家庭生活》这样的重启剧。

sentences.en: When we talk about Laugh Tracks now,
sentences.zh: 当我们现在谈论笑声轨时，

sentences.zh: 基本上都是在开它们的玩笑。

sentences.en: But when Paul was growing up and every show had a Laugh Track,
sentences.zh: 但在保罗成长、每个节目都有笑声轨的年代，

sentences.en: But as a TV critic, I've watched Laugh Tracks become contentious and deeply uncool.

sentences.en: It's always fascinated me that something we barely noticed for so long,

sentences.zh: 如果是这样，为什么我们花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: From Slate Magazine, this is Decoder Ring, a show about cracking cultural mysteries.
sentences.zh: 来自Slate杂志，这里是《解码环》，一档破解文化谜题的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Slate's TV critic, Willa Paskin, and every month, I'll take a cultural object, idea, or habit
sentences.zh: 我是Slate的电视评论人薇拉·帕斯金，每个月，我都会选取一个文化客体、理念或习惯，

sentences.en: and try to figure out where it comes from, what it means, and why it matters.
sentences.zh: 试图弄清它来自哪里，意味着什么，以及它为什么重要。

sentences.en: Today, what happened to the Laugh Track?
sentences.zh: 今天的话题：笑声轨怎么了？
想象一下，那是20世纪50年代。

sentences.en: You've just gotten your very first television set.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚买到了你的第一台电视机。

sentences.en: It weighs a ton, and it's the size of a bureau, with wood paneling and a couple of dials on the side.
sentences.zh: 它重得要命，有写字台那么大，带有木质面板，侧面还有几个旋钮。

sentences.en: You set it up in the living room, and you call in the whole family, and you turn it on.
sentences.zh: 你把它安装在客厅里，把全家人都叫过来，然后打开了它。

sentences.en: But ladies and gentlemen, I must tell you...
sentences.zh: 但是女士们先生们，我必须告诉你们……

sentences.en: Originally a hit radio show, the series starred Benny,
sentences.zh: 该系列最初是一档热门广播节目，由曾做过杂耍艺人和喜剧演员的本尼

sentences.en: a one-time vaudeville performer and comedian, as a version of himself, a radio star.
sentences.zh: 主演，他在剧中扮演自己版本的一个广播明星。

sentences.en: And now that show from the radio, it's on your television.
sentences.zh: 现在，那个广播里的节目，来到了你的电视上。

sentences.en: And even though you've heard it before, you've never seen anything like it.
sentences.zh: 尽管你以前听过，但你从未见过这样的场面。

sentences.en: Before, when you watched a performance, it was in public, with an audience,
sentences.zh: 以前，当你观看演出时，是在公共场合，有观众陪伴，

sentences.en: and now it's happening in your house.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一切正发生在你的家里。

sentences.en: Think about how strange, how new that must have been.
sentences.zh: 想想看，这该有多么奇怪，多么新奇。

sentences.en: Something that tells you what you're watching.
sentences.zh: 某种告诉你正在看什么的声音。

sentences.en: It was my sponsor who didn't have the nerve.
sentences.zh: 是我的赞助商没有这个胆量。

sentences.en: That's how most early TV comedies were recorded, in front of a live audience,
sentences.zh: 这就是早期大多数电视喜剧的录制方式，在现场观众面前录制，

sentences.en: oftentimes in studios in New York.
sentences.zh: 通常是在纽约的演播室里。

sentences.en: By the early 50s, as the TV industry moved away from New York and into Hollywood,
sentences.zh: 到50年代初，随着电视行业从纽约转移到好莱坞，

sentences.en: executives wanted to move away from this traditional approach
sentences.zh: 高管们希望摆脱这种传统的做法，

sentences.en: of broadcasting what amounted to live stage shows.
sentences.zh: 即播放等同于现场舞台秀的节目。

sentences.en: They wanted to shoot comedies on film.
sentences.zh: 他们希望用胶片拍摄喜剧。

sentences.en: Comedies that weren't live, but that still sounded live.
sentences.zh: 不是现场直播，但听起来依然像现场的喜剧。
解决这个问题的办法是什么？

sentences.en: And the person who came up with the solution?
sentences.zh: 想出这个办法的人是谁？

sentences.en: Douglas was a mechanical engineer who had worked on radar for the Navy in World War II,
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯是一名机械工程师，曾在二战期间为海军从事雷达研究，

sentences.en: so he knew his way around audio and electronics.
sentences.zh: 所以他精通音频和电子技术。

sentences.en: In 1950, The Hank McKeown Show, a mostly forgotten series from NBC,
sentences.zh: 1950年，NBC一部大体上已被遗忘的系列剧《汉克·麦基恩秀》，

sentences.en: had used a rudimentary laugh track.
sentences.zh: 曾使用过一种初级的笑声轨。

sentences.en: But by 1953, Douglas had developed a better way to insert a laugh into a show.
sentences.zh: 但到1953年，道格拉斯已经开发出了一种将笑声插入节目的更好方法。

sentences.en: If you've ever watched an old sitcom, you've almost certainly heard his work.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过任何老情景喜剧，你几乎肯定听过他的作品。

sentences.en: Now we lift up the dryers and see how their hair turned out.
sentences.zh: 现在我们掀开烘干机，看看他们的发型做得怎么样。

sentences.en: I asked Ron Simon, curator of television and radio at the Paley Center,
sentences.zh: 我问过佩利中心（前身为电视和广播博物馆）的电视和广播策展人罗恩·西蒙，

sentences.en: formerly the Museum of Television and Radio, what he knew.
Charlie Douglas took the concept of just adding laughter,
sentences.zh: 查理·道格拉斯采用了仅仅添加笑声的概念，

sentences.en: probably from a transcription disc, to create a machine that could do it.
sentences.zh: 大概是从转录唱片中获取，从而创造出一台能够做到这一点的机器。

sentences.en: And he created this little box using laughter from Marcel Marceau and from Red Skelton,
sentences.zh: 他利用来自马塞尔·马索以及红·斯克尔顿无声片段中的笑声，

sentences.en: from the silent sequences, and created tape loops that could then be injected into film comedy
sentences.zh: 制作了这个小盒子，并制成了可以注入到喜剧胶片中以制造笑声的磁带循环。

sentences.en: Douglas then poured over these laughs at his kitchen table night after night.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯随后日复一日、夜复一夜地在厨房桌子旁仔细研究这些笑声。

sentences.en: He spliced them into analog tape reels that could be played on a patented device
sentences.zh: 他把它们拼接进模拟磁带盘中，这些磁带盘可以在一台获得专利的设备上播放，

sentences.en: Douglas had built himself out of household appliances, organ parts, and vacuum tubes.
sentences.zh: 该设备是道格拉斯用家用电器、风琴零件和真空管自己组装的。

sentences.en: The device was about three feet tall, the shape of a filing cabinet,
sentences.zh: 这个设备大约三英尺高，形状像一个文件柜，

sentences.en: very heavy, and had slots for 32 reels, which could hold 10 laughs each.
sentences.zh: 非常重，有32个插槽，每个插槽可容纳10个笑声。

sentences.en: It was officially named the Audience Response Duplicator,
sentences.zh: 它被正式命名为“观众反应复制器”，

sentences.en: but it became known as the Laugh Box, and that's laugh, spelled in the Goofy 50s style, L-A-F-F.
sentences.zh: 但它更为人所知的名字是“笑声盒”（Laugh Box），这里的“笑”是用50年代滑稽风格拼写的L-A-F-F。

sentences.en: The Laugh Box is this weird machine that's closer to, we'll say, steampunk than it is to,
sentences.zh: 笑声盒是一个奇怪的机器，比起加法器来，

sentences.en: like an adding machine where you just press these dials.
sentences.zh: 比方说，它更接近于蒸汽朋克，而不仅仅是按按旋钮那么简单。

sentences.en: Eventually it would evolve into more of a typewriter thing where you would punch keys.
sentences.zh: 最终它演变成了一种类似打字机的东西，你可以通过敲击按键来操作。
笑声盒可以发出咯咯的笑声。

sentences.en: It could laugh with side relief.
sentences.zh: 它可以发出带有解嘲性质的笑声。

sentences.en: It even had a reel, controlled by the foot pedal, that was just titters, tiny little one-person laughs.
sentences.zh: 它甚至有一个由脚踏板控制的音轨，里面全都是傻笑，那种极轻微的单人笑声。

sentences.en: At its most sophisticated, the box had 320 laughs.
sentences.zh: 在其最复杂的时候，这个盒子拥有320种笑声。

sentences.en: It could play one laugh at a time by pressing one key,
sentences.zh: 按下单个键就可以播放一段笑声，

sentences.en: or by pressing multiple keys together, it could play a bunch of laughs at once.
sentences.zh: 或者通过同时按下多个键，它可以一次性播放一堆笑声。

sentences.en: So if he thought something was remotely funny, he'd say,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他觉得某个地方有点搞笑，他就会说，

sentences.en: let's have this guy laugh right here.
sentences.zh: 就在这儿加一段笑声吧。

sentences.en: And he'd just have that going.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会把效果加上去。

sentences.zh: 也许他回过头来看的时候会觉得，你知道吗，

sentences.en: that wasn't quite as funny as the producer's going to want it.
sentences.zh: 这好像没达到制片人想要的那种搞笑程度。

sentences.en: So maybe he would add a second sound like this.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能会再加第二种笑声，像这样。

sentences.en: And then he would add it all together and mix it together so you hear the full product.
sentences.zh: 然后他把这些全部加在一起并混合起来，你就能听到最终的成品了。

sentences.zh: 通常发生的情况是，制片人或导演来看他的工作，

sentences.zh: 然后说，你知道吗，这里需要更大声的笑声。

sentences.zh: 你能配一个更响亮的大笑吗？

sentences.zh: 因为笑声音效盒是由道格拉斯获得专利并手工制作的，

sentences.en: it wasn't like just anyone can make or use one.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是随便什么人都能制作或使用它们的。

sentences.en: There were only a handful of working models at a time,
sentences.zh: 当时正常工作的设备只有寥寥数台，

sentences.en: and he basically had a monopoly on the process.
sentences.zh: 他基本上垄断了整个流程。

sentences.zh: 到了20世纪60年代，几乎所有的情景喜剧都是单镜头剧集，

sentences.en: not many producers want to talk about and really actually talk about,
sentences.zh: 没多少制片人愿意公开谈论，甚至真正去讨论，

sentences.en: you know, how the last sausage was actually made.
sentences.zh: 你知道，香肠究竟是怎么做出来的。

sentences.en: Douglas hardly ever gave interviews or spoke about his work.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯几乎从不接受采访，也从不谈论他的工作。

sentences.en: A 1966 piece from TV Guide titled
sentences.zh: 1966年《电视指南》上的一篇文章，标题是

sentences.en: The Hollywood Sphinx and His Laugh Box,
sentences.zh: 《好莱坞的狮身人面像与他的笑声音效盒》，

sentences.en: in which the Sphinx is Douglas,
sentences.zh: 其中的狮身人面像指的就是道格拉斯，

sentences.en: describes the mystery surrounding the man and his device.
sentences.zh: 文中描述了这个男人及其设备周围的神秘色彩。

sentences.en: I want to say here that every knock on the laugh track that you've ever heard,
sentences.zh: 我想在这里说明，你们听过的每一个对笑声音轨的批评，

sentences.en: that it's fake, that it's corny, that it's cheating, that it's not funny,
sentences.zh: 说它是假的、俗气的、作弊的、不好笑的，

sentences.en: that it thinks audiences are dumb, people have been saying since the beginning.
sentences.zh: 说它把观众当成傻子，这些言论从一开始就存在。

sentences.en: And that's part of the reason for Douglas' silence.
sentences.zh: 这也是道格拉斯保持沉默的部分原因。

sentences.en: But listening to Douglas' laughs, hearing Paul try to recreate them,
sentences.zh: 但听着道格拉斯的笑声，听着保罗试图重现它们，

sentences.en: it changed how I thought about them.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我对它们的看法。

sentences.en: I've always prided myself on being open-minded about the laugh track.
sentences.zh: 我一直为自己对笑声音轨抱持开放心态而感到自豪。

sentences.en: A funny show is a funny show, with or without one.
sentences.zh: 一部有趣的剧就是有趣的剧，无论有没有笑声音轨。

sentences.en: But even so, I always thought of them as automated, mechanical.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我过去一直认为它们是自动化、机械化的。

sentences.en: But they aren't really that at all.
sentences.zh: 但它们其实根本不是那样的。

sentences.en: Charlie Douglas played his laugh box like it was an instrument, literally.
sentences.zh: 查理·道格拉斯演奏他的笑声音效盒就像在演奏一件乐器，毫不夸张。

sentences.en: A lot of people think it was just a bunch of laughs thrown into a tape machine
sentences.zh: 很多人以为这只是一堆放进磁带机里的笑声，
然后有人在按按钮而已。

sentences.en: I mean, he took it very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对此极其认真。

sentences.en: It was used in the late 60s and 70s, including in the pilot for MASH.
sentences.zh: 它在60年代末和70年代被广泛使用，包括在《陆军流动医院》的试播集中。

sentences.en: You hear the laughter tailing off at the end?
sentences.zh: 你听到结尾处渐渐变弱的笑声了吗？

sentences.en: It tells a story in a single laugh.
sentences.zh: 它用单一的笑声讲述了一个故事。

sentences.en: There's a joke, but one guy in the audience, he doesn't get it right away.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个笑话，但观众席里的某个人没有马上明白过来。

sentences.en: He's a split second late, and then he laughs a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 他慢了零点几秒，然后多笑了那么一小会儿。

sentences.en: Charlie Douglas wasn't just a sound engineer.
sentences.zh: 查理·道格拉斯不仅仅是一名声学工程师。

sentences.en: The rap on the laugh track is that it's fake laughter from a fake audience.
sentences.zh: 对笑声音轨的指责在于它是来自虚假观众的虚假笑声。

sentences.en: The laugh track doesn't just represent a bogus audience.
sentences.zh: 笑声音轨不仅仅代表虚假的观众。

sentences.en: It represents an audience of one, of Charlie Douglas.
sentences.zh: 它代表着一个由一人组成的观众，也就是查理·道格拉斯。

sentences.en: He definitely goosed laughs at producers' instructions,
sentences.zh: 他确实根据制片人的指示刻意夸大了笑声，

sentences.en: but to a large extent he and the people who worked for him followed their guts.
sentences.zh: 但在很大程度上，他和他的同事们还是凭直觉行事。

sentences.en: It's incredible that one man's taste and sense of humor were so important in pacing an entire type of television comedy.
sentences.zh: 真难以置信，一个人的品味和幽默感竟然对整整一种类型的电视喜剧的节奏起到了如此重要的作用。

sentences.en: So how did the laugh track-driven era of TV come to an end?
sentences.zh: 那么，由笑声音轨主导的电视时代是如何走向终结的呢？

sentences.en: How did the laugh track go from being a tittering companion to an annoyance?
sentences.zh: 笑声音轨是如何从一个窃笑的伴侣变成一种烦恼的？

sentences.en: To answer that, I think we need to think about the laugh track as not just a habit or an object,
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我认为我们需要将笑声音轨不仅仅视为一种习惯或物件，

sentences.en: but an idea, an idea about why we laugh.
sentences.zh: 而是一个理念，一个关于我们为什么会笑的理念。

sentences.en: I'm going to get to another idea about laughter later on,
sentences.zh: 我稍后会谈到关于笑声的另一个理念，

sentences.en: but this first one, I think it makes the laugh track of the 50s and 60s make a lot more sense.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得第一个理念能让50和60年代的笑声音轨变得更容易理解。

sentences.en: Here, I want you to listen to something, something that people once thought was really funny.
sentences.zh: 来，我想让你听点东西，这是人们曾经觉得非常好笑的东西。

sentences.en: That menacing sequence is from the OK Laughing Record.
sentences.zh: 那段带有威胁意味的音频片段出自《没关系笑声音片》。

sentences.en: OK, O-K-E-H, is the name of the record label that released it in 1922.
sentences.zh: OK，也就是 O-K-E-H，是1922年发行它的唱片公司的名字。

sentences.en: It was recorded a few years earlier in Germany,
sentences.zh: 它是在几年前于德国录制的，

sentences.en: and it's the sound of a cornet being interrupted by a hysterically laughing woman
sentences.zh: 声音内容是一段短号演奏被一个歇斯底里大笑的女人打断，

sentences.en: who was joined by a hysterically laughing man.
sentences.zh: 随后一个歇斯底里大笑的男人也加入了进来。

sentences.en: It goes on for two and a half minutes.
sentences.zh: 这段音频持续了两分半钟。

sentences.en: Two and a half creepy, creepy minutes.
sentences.zh: 整整两分半钟令人毛骨悚然的音频。

sentences.en: But in 1922, people thought it was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 但在1922年，人们觉得它滑稽极了。

sentences.en: The OK Laughing Record was a huge novelty hit.
sentences.zh: 《没关系笑声音片》是一个巨大的新奇热门唱片。

sentences.en: There's speculation it sold over a million copies.
sentences.zh: 据推测它的销量超过了一百万张。

sentences.en: It spawned an entire mini-genre of novelty laughing records.
sentences.zh: 它催生了一个全新的搞笑唱片微型流派。

sentences.en: The laugh track, it's a version of the OK Laughing Record.
sentences.zh: 笑声音轨其实就是《没关系笑声音片》的一个变体。

sentences.en: It's trying to make you laugh just by listening to other people laugh.
sentences.zh: 它试图仅仅通过让你听别人笑来让你发笑。

sentences.en: What's funny must be the laughter, because it's not the joke.
sentences.zh: 好笑的肯定得是笑声，因为笑话本身并不好笑。

sentences.en: But this particular approach to humor, it's not that popular right now.
sentences.zh: 但这种特定的幽默方式，现在已经不那么受欢迎了。

sentences.en: To find someone to defend it, I had to talk to one of Paul's friends, Ben Glenn.
sentences.zh: 为了找个人来为它辩护，我不得不采访保罗的朋友本·格伦。

sentences.en: He's an art historian by training, but he's also a devoted laugh track enthusiaSt.
sentences.zh: 他受过艺术史方面的专业训练，但同时也是一个狂热的笑声音轨爱好者。

sentences.en: He and Paul are in the same Charlie Douglas Facebook group.
sentences.zh: 他和保罗在同一个查理·道格拉斯的Facebook群组里。

sentences.en: If you think about a show that relies heavily on the laugh track like Bewitched or The Munsters,
sentences.zh: 如果你想一想那些极度依赖笑声音轨的节目，比如《家有仙妻》或《亚当斯一家》，

sentences.en: if you didn't have it, it just wouldn't be funny.
sentences.zh: 如果没有它，这节目就根本不好笑了。

sentences.en: But does that mean that show's just actually bad, and it was using this crutch?
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着这部剧本身其实很烂，而它一直在借助这种拐杖呢？
嗯，是的，是的，部分是这样。

sentences.en: But somebody getting a pie in the face and then there's silence is not funny, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果有人脸上挨了一派，然后全场一片死寂，这并不好笑，对吧？

sentences.en: Somebody getting the pie in the face with a huge laugh, that's funny.
sentences.zh: 如果有人脸上挨了一派，接着爆发出巨大的笑声，那就好笑了。

sentences.en: I found this, that does a tree falling in the forest make a sound, Zen Cohen of sitcom
sentences.zh: 我发现了一个问题，那就是“森林里树倒下有没有声音”这种情景喜剧笑声版的禅宗问题，

sentences.en: Is a pie in the face funny if no one laughs?
sentences.zh: 如果没人笑，脸部挨派好笑吗？

sentences.en: Is an episode of Friends funny if no one laughs?
sentences.zh: 如果没人笑，《老友记》的一集还好笑吗？

sentences.en: That's what I wondered after coming across this video, posted on YouTube by the user
sentences.zh: 这是我在YouTube用户SBOSS发布的无笑声音轨版《老友记》视频后，

sentences.en: SBOSS, of Friends without a laugh track.
Here's where I win all my money back.
sentences.zh: 这就是我把输掉的钱全都赢回来的时候。

sentences.en: You can hear what the rhythm of the show is supposed to be, how the pacing depends upon
sentences.zh: 你可以听到这部剧原本的节奏应该是怎样的，它的节奏是如何依赖于

sentences.en: Without it, Friends sounds weird and unnatural.
sentences.zh: 如果没有笑声，《老友记》听起来就会显得诡异而不自然。

sentences.en: If there's no audience laughter, it's suddenly stark how odd it is that the characters aren't
sentences.zh: 如果没有观众的笑声，角色们没有试图逗彼此笑这件事就会显得突兀而怪异。

sentences.en: trying to make each other laugh.
sentences.zh: 角色们没有试图逗彼此笑这件事就会显得突兀而怪异。

sentences.en: Friends needs its laughs to be funny, even if some of them are fake.
sentences.zh: 《老友记》需要它的笑声来保持搞笑，哪怕其中有些笑声是假的。

sentences.en: She's upstairs, not doing the dishes.
And I'll tell you something, you know, I'm not doing them this time.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说件事，你知道的，这次我才不洗呢。

sentences.en: I don't care if those dishes just sit in the sink until they're all covered with, I'll
sentences.zh: 我才不管那些盘子是不是就堆在水槽里直到全都长满，等我回家我再

sentences.en: do them when I get home.
The transition away from the laugh track started slowly.
sentences.zh: 摆脱笑声音轨的过渡是一个缓慢的过程。

sentences.en: In the 70s, with Norman Lear sitcoms like All in the Family, comedy started to be taped
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，随着诺曼·利尔制作的《全家福》等情景喜剧的出现，喜剧开始重新回到

sentences.en: in front of a live studio audience again.
sentences.zh: 有现场录影观众的面前拍摄。

sentences.en: The audience's laughs would be smoothed out, edited, or boosted.
sentences.zh: 观众的笑声会被平滑处理、剪辑或增强。

sentences.en: This is a process called sweetening, which Douglas had done a lot of, and it still happens
sentences.zh: 这是一个被称为“甜化”的过程，道格拉斯曾大量运用这种技术，而且这种做法

sentences.en: But the aim, already, was that the laughs should sound more realistic.
sentences.zh: 但当时的目标已经是让笑声听起来更加逼真了。

sentences.en: In the 80s and 90s, some shows, like The Wonder Years, The Larry Sanders Show, and The Days
sentences.zh: 在80和90年代，一些剧集，比如《纯真年代》、《拉里·桑德斯秀》和《莫莉·多德的日日夜夜》，

sentences.en: and Nights of Molly Dodd, started to experiment with dropping the laugh track.
sentences.zh: 开始尝试取消笑声音轨。

sentences.en: But TV's biggest hits, shows like Cheers, Seinfeld, and Friends, still had them.
sentences.zh: 但电视上最热门的节目，如《干杯酒吧》、《宋飞传》和《老友记》，依然保留着笑声。

sentences.en: By the late 90s, with the rise of cable and un-laugh-tracked animated series like The
sentences.zh: 到90年代末，随着有线电视的兴起以及没有笑声音轨的动画片《辛普森一家》的出现，

sentences.en: Simpsons, even the network started contemplating making different kinds of comedies, setting
sentences.zh: 甚至各大电视网也开始考虑制作不同类型的喜剧，这就引发了

sentences.en: up a collision between the old idea about comedy, and the typical way of doing things,
sentences.zh: 旧的喜剧观念与传统制作方式之间的冲突，

sentences.en: and a new idea about comedy, and a new way of shooting a TV show.
sentences.zh: 并与新的喜剧观念和全新的电视节目拍摄方式产生了碰撞。
被卷入这场冲突之中的是什么呢？
那就是阿伦·索尔金的《体育之夜》。

sentences.en: You're watching Sports Night on CSC, so come on back.
sentences.zh: 你正在收看CSC频道的《体育之夜》，请不要走开。

sentences.en: Two and a half minutes back.
In 1997, Sorkin sold Sports Night, his first TV show, to ABC.
sentences.zh: 1997年，索尔金将他的第一部电视剧《体育之夜》卖给了美国广播公司。

sentences.en: It was a comedy, set behind the scenes of an ESPN-style sports network.
sentences.zh: 这是一部以ESPN风格的体育电视网幕后为背景的喜剧。

sentences.en: Sorkin and the director, Tommy Shlami, wanted to shoot it like a single-camera show.
sentences.zh: 索尔金和导演汤米·施拉米希望像拍摄单镜头剧集那样来拍它。

sentences.en: The set had four walls, the camera moved, and they wanted to shoot it without a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 布景有四面墙，摄像机会移动，而且他们希望在拍摄时不要加入笑声音轨。

sentences.en: They wanted to do something different, but not that different.
sentences.zh: 他们想做点不一样的，但又没那么大胆。

sentences.en: The economics of television, and certainly half-hour television,
sentences.zh: 电视的经济学，尤其是半小时时长的电视剧，

sentences.en: was so massive for shows that had had traditional laugh tracks that they were really very nervous about giving that up completely.
sentences.zh: 对于那些采用传统罐头笑声的节目来说影响太大了，以至于他们对彻底放弃这种做法感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: What did you feel like the laugh track meant about your show?
sentences.zh: 你觉得罐头笑声对你的节目意味着什么？

sentences.en: The sort of base tone of a situational comedy is the laugh track.
sentences.zh: 情景喜剧的基本基调就是罐头笑声。

sentences.en: I think we're familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都对此很熟悉。

sentences.en: I think it sort of resonates in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它在某种程度上会引发共鸣。

sentences.en: But I think it is kind of establishing a conceptual idea about a show that is saying, it's not real.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得它其实是在为节目树立一个概念，也就是在告诉观众：这不是真的。

sentences.en: I'm there with this group of people.
That was not the idea of the way I think Aaron wrote or what I think Sports Night was about.
sentences.zh: 这并不是艾伦的写作理念，也不是我所理解的《体育之夜》的内核。

sentences.en: Here's a clip of the laugh track from the Sports Night pilot.
sentences.zh: 这是《体育之夜》试播集中罐头笑声的一个片段。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the point I'm making is that I can't...
sentences.zh: 对，但我想说的是，我不能……

sentences.en: Oh, you're here for the associate producer job.
sentences.zh: 哦，你是来应聘助理制片人的。

sentences.en: Yes, and let me just say that it is an extraordinary...
sentences.zh: 是的，我只想说这是一个极其……

sentences.en: Sports Night was one of the first shows where, as a viewer, I could really feel that the laugh track was holding the show back.
sentences.zh: 《体育之夜》是最早的一批节目，作为观众，我能明显感觉到罐头笑声在拖后腿。

sentences.en: It doesn't want to pause to wait for the audience's laughter.
sentences.zh: 它不想停下来等待观众的笑声。

sentences.en: So the laughs have to be shoehorned into the rare breaks in Sorkin's dense dialogue, where they sound even faker than usual.
sentences.zh: 所以笑声只能硬生生地塞进索金那些密集对白中仅有的间隙里，听上去比平时更加虚假。

sentences.en: Dispatches from a whole other sensibility.
sentences.zh: 来自完全不同审美品味的传真。

sentences.en: What you can hear starting to happen with Sports Night is the laugh track changing from background noise into an impediment.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到《体育之夜》开始发生的变化：罐头笑声正从背景噪音变成一种阻碍。

sentences.en: It's actively keeping Sports Night from being as funny and fast, from being as good as it could be.
sentences.zh: 它在很大程度上妨碍了《体育之夜》应有的幽默与紧凑，阻碍了它达到原本可以达到的高度。

sentences.en: After its first few episodes, Sports Night stopped being taped in front of an audience at all, and the laughter got even fainter.
sentences.zh: 在前几集之后，《体育之夜》彻底取消了现场观众录制，笑声也变得更加微弱了。

sentences.en: Here's a clip from an episode at the end of season one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一季末尾一集的一个片段。
你现在信号断断续续的。

sentences.en: Now you're not there at all.
For its second season, ABC let the show drop the laugh track entirely.
sentences.zh: 到了第二季，ABC允许该节目彻底抛弃了罐头笑声。

sentences.en: But it was canceled at the end of that season anyway, in 2000, just ever so slightly ahead of its time.
sentences.zh: 但它还是在该季末的2000年被砍掉了，比时代稍微超前了一点点。

sentences.en: The laugh track-free British version of The Office premiered in 2001.
sentences.zh: 没有罐头笑声的英国版《办公室》于2001年首播。

sentences.en: In 2003, Arrested Development started airing on Fox.
sentences.zh: 2003年，《发展受阻》开始在福克斯电视台播出。

sentences.en: In 2005, the American adaptation of The Office started airing on NBC, the first huge hit without a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 2005年，美国改编版的《办公室》开始在全国广播公司播出，这是第一部没有罐头笑声的超级大热门。

sentences.en: That same year, Everybody Loves Raymond won the Emmy for Best Comedy.
sentences.zh: 同年，《人人都爱雷蒙德》获得了艾美奖最佳喜剧奖。

sentences.en: That's the last time a sitcom with a laugh track has done so.
sentences.zh: 这也是带罐头笑声的情景喜剧最后一次获此殊荣。

sentences.en: The end of the laugh track era.
I want to talk about another theory about laughter that's different from the pie-in-the-face theory I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈另一种关于笑声的理论，它不同于我之前提到的“拿派砸脸”理论。

sentences.en: In this theory, laughter isn't a fundamentally social activity, something that we do just because everyone else is doing it.
sentences.zh: 在这种理论中，笑并非一种根本上的社交活动，不是那种因为别人都在笑而跟着笑的行为。

sentences.en: It's something deeply, wonderfully individual and idiosyncratic, a reaction to the quality of the joke itself.
sentences.zh: 它是一种深刻、奇妙且极具个人特色与特质的反应，是对笑话本身质量的真实反馈。

sentences.en: Representing this point of view is the TV writer Andy Secunda.
sentences.zh: 电视编剧安迪·塞昆达正是这种观点的代表人物。

sentences.en: Andy's now a writer on the current ABC sitcom The Goldbergs, which doesn't have a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 安迪目前是ABC正在热播的情景喜剧《戈德堡一家》的编剧，这部剧没有罐头笑声。

sentences.en: But his first show, the 2004 UPN sitcom Love Incorporated, about modern-day matchmakers, did.
sentences.zh: 但他的第一部作品——2004年UPN电视台关于现代媒人的情景喜剧《爱情公司》——是有的。

sentences.en: I'm talking about $10,000 to help improve the human condition.
sentences.zh: 我说的是能改善人类状况的一万美元。

sentences.en: Well, $10,000 will help improve this human's condition very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，一万美元能大大改善这个人类的状况。

sentences.en: Before working on Love Incorporated, Andy had been a writer for Conan and a teacher and performer at the improv comedy powerhouse Upright Citizens Brigade.
sentences.zh: 在参与《爱情公司》之前，安迪曾是柯南的编剧，也是即兴喜剧重镇“正义公民大联盟”的导师和演员。

sentences.en: I was an alternative comedy snob, and coming out of the New York scene, already was, like, every show with a laugh track other than Seinfeld is, you know, passe, a dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 我曾是个另类喜剧 snob（精英主义者），从纽约的喜剧圈出来时，就已经觉得除了《宋飞传》之外，所有带罐头笑声的节目都过时了，像个老古董。

sentences.en: But Andy didn't have the clout to keep Love Incorporated from having a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 但安迪当时没有足够的影响力来阻止《爱情公司》使用罐头笑声。

sentences.en: The show was performed in front of a studio audience, and they had some real laughs.
sentences.zh: 这个节目是在演播室现场观众面前表演的，他们也确实发出了一些真实的笑声。

sentences.en: But then a sound editor came in to sweeten it, boosting and manipulating all of them.
sentences.zh: 但随后音效剪辑师介入进行了“润色”，对所有的笑声进行了增强和操纵。

sentences.en: So the real laughs were replaced by a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 于是，真实的笑声被罐头笑声所取代。

sentences.en: But Andy didn't want to use that laugh track in the typical way.
sentences.zh: 但安迪并不想以典型的方式使用这些罐头笑声。

sentences.en: So I guess my take was, well, since we're doing this anyway, why don't we just decide what's funny?
sentences.zh: 所以我的想法是，既然我们无论如何都在这么做，为什么不由我们来决定什么是好笑的呢？

sentences.en: To me, I was like, well, it's going to be this creation, this false thing.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，我觉得这既然是一个人为创作的虚假产物，

sentences.en: Just make the whole thing a fiction.
sentences.zh: 干脆把整个东西都变成纯粹的虚构。

sentences.en: I want to train the audience that's watching at home who's not really paying that much attention anyway, in my head.
sentences.zh: 我想在我的脑海里训练那些坐在电视机前、本来也没怎么专心看的观众。

sentences.en: In other words, Andy wanted to rig the laugh track to reflect what was really funny.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，安迪想要操控罐头笑声，来反映真正好笑的内容。

sentences.en: He understood how the laugh track is supposed to work, that it's supposed to make people laugh at what other people are laughing at.
sentences.zh: 他理解罐头笑声原本的作用，也就是让人跟着别人的笑声一起笑。

sentences.en: But he wanted to retrofit it to account for the second theory of laughter, to tell audiences, hey, some jokes are just funnier than others, and you should laugh at those.
sentences.zh: 但他想要对其进行改造，以适应第二种笑声理论，以此告诉观众：嘿，有些笑话就是比别的更好笑，你们应该为这些笑。

sentences.en: But even so, you can see, he may be skeptical of the laughter of the crowd, but he believes in the objective quality of the joke.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，你可以看出，他或许对大众的笑声持怀疑态度，但他坚信笑话本身的客观品质。

sentences.en: You may be able to get a big laugh out of an audience and be not that great a comic.
sentences.zh: 你也许能从观众那里博得大笑，但你未必是个多么优秀的喜剧演员。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of comics would argue, well, if you get the laugh, then you are a great comic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，许多喜剧演员会争辩说，只要你能逗笑观众，那你就是个伟大的喜剧演员。

sentences.en: I disagree, because I'm a snob.
sentences.zh: 我不同意，因为我是个精英主义者。

sentences.en: Andy may be a snob, but his perspective has become widespread.
sentences.zh: 安迪或许是个精英主义者，但他的观点已经变得非常普遍。

sentences.en: This is how lots of people think about comedy now.
sentences.zh: 现在很多人都是这样看待喜剧的。

sentences.en: Some jokes just are better than others, and you can't tell simply based on what got the biggest laugh, especially when that laugh comes from a laugh track.
sentences.zh: 有些笑话就是比别的更好，你不能仅仅根据哪个笑声最大来判断，尤其是当那个笑声来自罐头音轨时。

sentences.en: For decades, TV was ruled by this idea that laughter is socially contingent, and then that idea was surpassed by this other idea, that laughter is idiosyncratic and individual.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，电视一直被“笑声是由社交决定的”这一观念统治，后来这一观念又被另一种观念超越，即“笑声是个人化且独特的”。

sentences.en: But this was a big transition.
sentences.zh: 但这是一次巨大的转变。

sentences.en: For some viewers, the laugh track didn't just stop encouraging laughter.
sentences.zh: 对于某些观众来说，罐头笑声不仅不再鼓励欢笑，

sentences.en: Today, shows with laugh tracks have been almost entirely cut out of the critical conversation.

sentences.en: But they still have their modern-day defenders and uses, especially in the revivals of beloved shows that had laugh tracks, like Will & Grace.

sentences.en: And the laugh track, it helped us to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 而罐头笑声，它曾帮助我们走到了这一步。

sentences.en: For a long time, the laugh track seemed permanent,
